title: On the Cliffs
content:
I’m dying. I can feel it.

The clouds at the horizon reflect the afterglow of the setting sun; autumn in Pittsburgh remains cool and crisp. The brilliant city lights and the roar of machinery make it feel as though this city has caught "The New York Fever."

Does this world truly have anything to do with me? The heavy traffic, the sunrises and sunsets—it seems the world doesn't care who is missing. After all, this is just a pale blue, lonely dot. All the "good" and "bad" are merely our own wishful thinking.

This is truly a strange place. Society is like a giant pendulum, swinging through the void, generating beauty and ugliness, high and low, meaning and purpose.

*Click, click, click, click.* The traffic light counts down. Perhaps this is what dying feels like. Sinking deeper and deeper, I reach out with a thousand hands, searching for a branch to save my life, clutching it tight and praying it doesn't snap too soon.

Rock, rap, cigarettes, alcohol, literature, art. These elements and labels are like nails, pinning seven billion people firmly to the cliffside, keeping them from plummeting into the abyss.

I hope you find your own nail on this precipice, too.
